prompt:
A 30-second cinematic episode of an epic space-exploration saga, awe-inspiring and breathtaking, like a nature documentary crossed with a sci-fi epic. This is an ALIEN world — it must never look like Antarctica or any Earth snowfield.

The hero: the sleek ice-white robot with the black racing-helmet visor from the first reference image; its fighter-jet form is shown from several angles in the following reference images — note the sharp pointed nose at the front and the engine exhausts at the rear. The golden glyph cube artifact is the last reference image.

LIGHTING RULE: one distant blue-white sun lights everything; consistent light direction and hard shadows in every shot. No moons, and no other round body in the sky.

FLIGHT RULE: whenever the jet flies, it always flies NOSE-FIRST — the sharp pointed nose leads in the direction of travel, engines trailing blue fire. It banks and carves like a real aircraft, never drifting sideways or backwards.

THE WORLD — the Stillwater: a world whose entire ocean froze in a single instant. Its ice is not white snow but deep blue-black glass, so clear that the drowned landscape is visible far below through it. Every wave was caught mid-break and stands frozen hundreds of metres tall, and — the impossible part — the spray those waves threw up is still hanging in the air, millions of suspended crystal beads that never landed, glittering in mid-flight exactly where the instant caught them.

STILLNESS RULE: nothing on this world falls and nothing drifts. The suspended spray hangs perfectly motionless in the air and stays motionless even as the jet tears past it, parting only in the wake and then hanging still again. There is no wind, no snowfall, no cloud, no aurora — the sky is clear black with stars and the single blue-white sun.

OPENING (0-3s): deep space. The robot drifts in orbit above a dark glassy blue-black sphere webbed with pale stress-lines like a struck marble, the frozen wave-fronts visible from orbit as vast curved ridges — visibly NOT Earth. A small golden holographic counter floats beside its helmet reading exactly "FRAGMENT 001 / 512". The robot dives.

THE DIVE (3-16s): mid-fall the robot transforms into its fighter-jet form and drops nose-first through the field of hanging crystal beads, which part in its wake and then hang still again. A sweeping continuous flyover: threading the curl of a single colossal frozen wave, blue-black and glass-clear, with the drowned world faintly visible through it; then racing low over a plain of glass where a shoal of enormous unknown creatures is frozen in place beneath the surface, mid-turn, perfectly preserved; then between spires where a waterfall stopped in mid-plunge and now stands as a solid twisted column; and finally the landmark — the Stillwater Eye, a perfectly circular disc of flawless mirror ice a kilometre across, so smooth it reflects the stars whole. Fast, fluid, majestic — no slow motion.

THE CHALLENGE (16-23s): the jet transforms back into the robot and lands on the mirror. Deep beneath the glass, a golden light pulses. The robot drives a fist into the ice — and the whole disc shatters into vast tilting plates, the suspended spray above it finally released and falling all at once in a glittering curtain. It leaps plate to plate as they rear and slide, one plate flips and drops it toward the black water, it catches a rearing edge one-handed, hauls itself up, and rides a tilting slab down toward the glow.

THE FRAGMENT (23-28s): in the dark water at the heart of the broken mirror, the artifact from the reference image — a single fist-sized golden metallic cube etched with glowing circuit glyphs — rises slowly on a column of light. The robot catches it in both hands. The glyphs flare, and for one breathtaking beat every suspended bead of spray still hanging across the whole frozen ocean lights gold at once, a galaxy of tiny stars stretching to the horizon.

THE RITUAL CLOSE (28-30s): close-up on the robot's open palm holding the ONE cube — there is only ever this single cube on screen. Its glyphs pulse and golden holographic text appears in the air beside it reading exactly "FRAGMENT — SECURED" (this exact text, two words only, NO numbers or digits anywhere in it). A calm, epic voice speaks the episode's only words: "Fragment one... secured." Final frame holds on the robot and the single glowing cube, the shattered mirror glittering behind it.

LYRIC RULE: the singer sings ONLY the four quoted lyric lines below, exactly as written — never any other words. Scene descriptions in this prompt are camera directions, NOT lyrics, and must never be sung or spoken. The final spoken line must be clean, with no other words attached to it.

Audio: the soundtrack is an original epic MOTIVATIONAL anthem with clear English vocals, composed for this episode — soaring and uplifting, drums building through the dive and peaking as the fragment is taken. The voice sings these lyrics across the episode, timed to the action:

"A whole world stopped but I keep moving on,
I'll break the quiet where the light has gone!
Frozen ocean, you can't hold me down —
I'm the one thing here that's still around!"

The sung anthem is the only sound until the end, where a calm epic voice speaks the single line "Fragment one... secured." No other dialogue, no robotic servo sounds. Vertical 9:16 composition, cinematic lighting, photoreal detail on the landscapes, the robot always crisp and readable. Fast-paced, majestic, unforgettable.
